hero.headline: Flooding blocks SW Dyer Point Road in Palm City; deputies deploy high-water vehicles
hero.body:
King tide flooding made SW Dyer Point Road in Palm City impassable Monday, prompting Martin County Sheriff’s Office deputies to bring in three high-water vehicles to help reach people stranded in vehicles or homes. The flooding came as a coastal flood warning remained in effect for coastal Martin County through 2 a.m. Thursday.

Flooding also was reported on SW 34th Street and Cornell Avenue. One driver described water about waist-deep in part of the area. Resident Terresa Baldwin said water surrounded the front and back of her home and described Monday’s flooding as the worst she had seen in eight years. Baldwin also raised concerns about the water’s smell and said she believed it contained sewage rather than only runoff.

The National Weather Service’s coastal flood warning covers low-lying areas near the water in Palm Beach, Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. The warning runs through 2 a.m. Thursday in coastal Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties and through 8 p.m. Wednesday in coastal Palm Beach County. More high tides were expected through Wednesday, with Monday’s high tide forecast for 9:06 p.m.

Deputies urged people to avoid flooded areas and not to drive through standing water. The sheriff’s office advised residents to call 911 if they need emergency assistance.

hero.headline: Coastal flood warning covers St. Lucie County through 2 a.m. Thursday
hero.body:
A coastal flood warning remains in effect for coastal St. Lucie County until 2 a.m. Thursday as king tides are expected to produce the season’s highest tides along Florida’s Atlantic coast. Low-lying locations close to the water are at risk of flooding, particularly where drainage is poor and around high tide. According to the National Weather Service, coastal Martin and Indian River counties are also under the warning until 2 a.m. Thursday. The warning for coastal Palm Beach County lasts until 8 p.m. Wednesday. Monday’s highest tide is expected at 9:06 p.m.

In Palm City, flooding has made SW Dyer Point Road impassable, the Martin County Sheriff’s Office reported. Flooding was also reported on SW 34th Street and Cornell Avenue. Images released by the Sheriff’s Office show widespread water across streets, with people walking through water reaching their ankles. The agency is sending high-water rescue vehicles to assist people stranded in homes or vehicles. Residents should stay away from the flooded area and call 911 if they need emergency help. Drivers should never attempt to cross a flooded road and should turn around instead. A separate video shows flooding on Indian River Drive, with a car traveling through the water.

In Boynton Beach, heavy flooding has closed the intersection of Ocean Avenue and Federal Highway. Drivers are being asked to stay clear of the intersection and take other routes. Officials plan to provide an update after the water drops and the intersection reopens. High tides have also forced the closure of Ocean Inlet Marina. Midtown Beach is temporarily closed because large surf and unusually high tides have made beach access unsafe, officials said. On South Ocean Boulevard, the northbound lane between Chilean Avenue and Australian Avenue will close from 10 a.m. to noon so crews can move a lifeguard tower.

Other coastal recreation areas are also affected. Delray Beach officials say red flags are flying at the city’s beach because of high surf and flooding. The Juno Beach Pier is closed until further notice after sustaining damage from a recent offshore surge and high surf. Those closures accompany the coastal flood warnings covering Palm Beach, Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. With flooding more likely near high tide, residents in low-lying waterfront areas and places with poor drainage should avoid flooded roads. The safety message for motorists is to turn back rather than drive into floodwater.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge dies while on duty Oct. 24
hero.teaser: Austin Hodge served at Station 9 and had been with the district for more than nine years. The district will share memorial arrangements as they are finalized.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge died while on duty Saturday, Oct. 24, the St. Lucie County Fire District announced, calling his death a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Hodge was assigned to Station 9 and had served the community for more than nine years after joining the district on July 17, 2017. Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue also shared condolences following his unexpected death Saturday morning. The circumstances surrounding his death have not been released.

Hodge’s death came more than a year after his younger brother, Jarius Hodge, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died on July 22, 2025, at age 26. The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. Austin had described Jarius as his best friend and said they enjoyed working alongside each other. He described his younger brother as someone who loved his family, his community and his country, loved going to work and pushed Austin to keep going.

Austin had said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025. According to Austin’s account, Jarius went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22 because he was struggling to breathe and died hours later. Austin said his brother had been healthy before becoming ill. He alleged that medical staff made critical errors while treating Jarius, including taking three attempts to intubate him. Those claims were allegations Austin raised while seeking accountability for his brother’s death.

Austin also spoke publicly about Florida’s medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability. He emphasized that the family wanted the physicians held accountable rather than financial compensation. Following Austin’s death, the St. Lucie County Fire District asked the public to respect his family as they grieve. The district said information about memorial arrangements would be shared as details are finalized. It also said additional information about ways to honor his service would be shared in coordination with his family.

hero.headline: Donalds, Jolly outline differences on taxes, schools and data centers in Florida race
hero.body:
Republican Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly outlined different approaches to property-tax revenue, school accountability and data centers in closing interviews as they campaigned across Florida. Ron DeSantis, while Jolly, who served in Congress as a Republican during the 2010s, is emphasizing housing, health care and education.

He said that work would be important if voters approve Amendment 3, which would raise homestead tax exemptions and reduce local revenue. hero.headline: Fort Pierce firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge, 34, dies on duty
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District confirmed that firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge, 34, died Saturday morning while on duty. Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, and was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce.

A procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies traveled from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce on Saturday morning. The district said it will share information about memorial arrangements and opportunities to honor Hodge’s service in coordination with his family as plans are finalized.

“His death is a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community,” the agency said. “The District extends its heartfelt condolences to Hodge’s family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time.” The district also thanked the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties for supporting its firefighters and helping honor Hodge.

Hodge’s younger brother, Jarius Hodge, also served with the St. Lucie County Fire District. He died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at work at Station 3. His family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. People gathered May 30 for a cookout and balloon release to celebrate what would have been his 27th birthday.

Austin Hodge spoke about his brother’s influence at that gathering. “He was a quiet leader, and we take a lot from him. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today.”

hero.headline: Florida approves USAA auto insurance rate cuts averaging 7% for over 498,000 policies
hero.body:
Florida Insurance Commissioner Mike Yaworsky has approved USAA Group auto insurance rate reductions averaging 7% across more than 498,000 policies statewide, according to the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation. The approvals cover several auto insurance programs, with savings varying by program.

Average rate decreases range from 0.4% to 11.2%, according to the state. USAA has its highest concentration of Florida business in Brevard, Escambia and Okaloosa counties. Average reductions in those counties are 5.8% in Brevard, 8% in Escambia and 8.4% in Okaloosa.

“The Office of Insurance Regulation is constantly reaching out to insurers to inquire about rate relief, and USAA is always stepping up to the plate and looking out for their consumers,” Yaworsky said in a release. He also encouraged other insurers to consider additional rate reductions.

Florida Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia characterized the reductions as another sign of improvement in the state's insurance market and credited Florida's tort reforms. “These auto insurance rate decreases will help Florida families keep more of their hard-earned money in their pockets, especially our military families,” Ingoglia said.

The latest approvals follow other savings USAA provided to Florida members over the past year. Between December 2025 and July 2026, the company provided nearly $1 billion in rate reductions and direct member returns, according to the release. That total included a $500 million dividend distributed to approximately 830,000 members.

State regulators also reported that Florida's five largest auto insurance groups have a combined indicated rate change of negative 12.6% for 2026. Those companies represent 81% of the state's auto insurance market, according to the release. The state also reported that Florida's personal auto liability loss ratio was 52.5% in 2025, the lowest in the nation and Florida's lowest level in 15 years.

hero.headline: Missing 5-year-old Mayra Glory Odelus found dead in water in Fort Pierce
hero.body:
Mayra Glory Odelus, a 5-year-old girl reported missing in Fort Pierce, was found dead in a nearby body of water Saturday afternoon, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department.

Mayra was reported missing at approximately 11:39 a.m. In an update issued at 4:13 p.m., the department said officers were at the scene after she was found dead in the water.

“Our deepest condolences are with Mayra’s family and loved ones during this tragic time,” police said.

hero.headline: Jensen Beach High School standout Andrew Burnette gains another year at Louisiana Tech
hero.body:
Former Jensen Beach High School standout Andrew Burnette has gained another season of football at Louisiana Tech after hiring a lawyer and challenging the NCAA over his eligibility. Burnette had exhausted his eligibility after his first season at the Division I level and spent a few months working with his father at a steel mill in Detroit. A change in NCAA eligibility rules this summer opened a path for him to seek one final year on the field.

Burnette moved from Michigan around age 12 and played football in Martin County. At Jensen Beach High School, wrestling initially drew him to the school. “I wasn't zoned for that school, but I went there for wrestling originally; that was my first passion,” said Burnette. As he progressed through high school, his focus shifted toward football. He established himself on the football field but struggled to attract college recruiters. “One of my main struggles was recruitment out of high school, because I felt like our area was a little under-recruited,” he said.

He began his college career at Highland Community College in Kansas, where he played nine games and rushed for 340 yards and two touchdowns. He then transferred to Independence Junior College, where he was cut from the team. Burnette contacted Keiser University in West Palm Beach, which had offered him a chance to play while he was in high school. A coach reviewed his film and invited him to join the program. Over two years at Keiser, Burnette rushed for more than 2,300 yards and 30 touchdowns, drawing interest from Division I programs, starting with Louisiana Tech.

After his first season at Louisiana Tech, Burnette returned to Michigan to work with his father. This summer, the NCAA announced the 5-in-5 rule, allowing student-athletes to compete for up to five seasons within a continuous five-year period. Burnette hired a lawyer and went to court against the NCAA before receiving another year of eligibility. “It was amazing; I would rather play football than do anything, and for me to have this opportunity again, it's a blessing,” he said.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County firefighter Austin Hodge, 34, dies while on duty
hero.body:
St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge, 34, died Saturday morning while on duty, the St. Lucie County Fire District said. Hodge was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce and had been with the district since July 17, 2017. Firefighters and personnel from other agencies took part in a procession Saturday morning from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce. The district described his death as a significant loss for its personnel and the broader fire service community. It offered condolences to his family, friends and fellow firefighters and said memorial arrangements would be announced as plans are completed with his family.

Hodge’s death came about a year after the death of his younger brother, Jarius Hodge, who also served with the St. Lucie County Fire District. Jarius died July 22, 2025, after becoming ill while working at Station 3. His family said he had the flu and felt weak before being rushed to a hospital, where he died hours later. On May 30, people gathered for a cookout and balloon release to mark what would have been his 27th birthday. Austin Hodge reflected on his brother’s influence at that gathering: “He was a quiet leader, and we take a lot from him. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today.”

The district thanked the St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties. It said their assistance helped ensure Hodge was treated with dignity and respect. hero.headline: Fort Pierce firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge, 34, dies while on duty
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge, 34, died Saturday morning while on duty, the agency said. Hodge worked at Station 9 in Fort Pierce and had served with the district since July 17, 2017. Firefighters and personnel from other public safety agencies accompanied him in a procession from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce that morning. The district described his death as a major loss for its personnel and the wider fire service community, and offered condolences to his family, friends and fellow firefighters.

Hodge’s death came about a year after the death of his younger brother, Jarius Hodge, who also worked for the district. Jarius died July 22, 2025, after becoming ill while working at Station 3. His family said he had the flu and felt weak before he was taken to a hospital, where he died hours later. On May 30, people gathered for a cookout and balloon release to mark what would have been his 27th birthday. Austin attended the gathering and spoke about the example his younger brother had set for him, particularly through his patience and calm leadership.

“He was a quiet leader, and we take a lot from him. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today,” Austin Hodge said at the birthday gathering. Another district firefighter, Connor Whitehead, 21, died May 31. The district has 20 fire stations and 523 firefighters, according to its website. Following Austin’s death, the agency thanked its firefighters, Honor Guard and public safety partners for coming together to honor him and support those who had served alongside him.

The district specifically recognized the St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties. It said their assistance helped ensure Hodge was treated with dignity and respect while providing support to fellow first responders. Other agencies offering condolences included the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Riviera Beach Fire Rescue. The district also expressed gratitude for the community’s support. It said details about memorial arrangements and opportunities to honor Hodge’s service will be announced in coordination with his family as plans are finalized.

cards.headline: Man dies after medical distress at Fort Pierce Service Plaza on Florida's Turnpike
cards.teaser: FHP said the man died at a hospital after being found unresponsive Sunday morning. Investigators do not suspect foul play.
cards.body:
A man who suffered medical distress Sunday morning at Fort Pierce Service Plaza on Florida's Turnpike died after being taken to a hospital, the Florida Highway Patrol said.

FHP units from Post 5 found the man at 5:40 a.m. He was unresponsive, was not breathing and had no pulse. He was transported to Florida Coast Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead, FHP said.

People traveling with the man said he had not been feeling well. FHP said no foul play is suspected in his death.

hero.headline: Jensen Beach captures District 13-4A football title against Fort Pierce Westwood
hero.body:
Jensen Beach faced Fort Pierce Westwood on Friday with the District 13-4A football championship at stake, seeking its fourth district title in five years. The Falcons entered the matchup after a 51-0 victory over Legacy the previous week, a shutout highlighted by two defensive touchdowns from senior linebacker Alex Thornton. The district contest put Jensen Beach among the Treasure Coast teams playing for championship honors on a night that also brought a title-winning performance from Vero Beach. For the Falcons, the matchup with Westwood offered an opportunity to add another championship to their recent run of district success.

Thornton supplied two of the biggest plays in Jensen Beach’s win over Legacy, returning a pair of interceptions for touchdowns. His scoring returns were part of a performance in which the Falcons held their opponent scoreless while putting up 51 points. That result gave Jensen Beach momentum heading into its meeting with Fort Pierce Westwood, where the stakes shifted to the district championship. The Falcons’ pursuit of a fourth title in five years was a central storyline entering Friday’s game, following a week in which their defense contributed both points and a shutout.

Vero Beach secured the District 8-6A championship by defeating rival Treasure Coast 24-0 on Friday. The Fighting Indians’ defense kept Treasure Coast off the scoreboard, continuing its strong play late in the season. The victory stretched Vero Beach’s winning streak to six games and added a district championship to that run. Vero Beach had been pursuing a third straight district title, and the shutout against its rival continued the program’s sustained success in district competition. While Jensen Beach entered its matchup seeking another championship, Vero Beach delivered a title-clinching result with a three-touchdown margin and a clean defensive performance against Treasure Coast.

Elsewhere in the region, lightning affected the Friday schedule in Palm Beach County. Delays pushed back the start of play, but Dwyer and Royal Palm Beach eventually got underway. Benjamin was also in action at home, where its promising young players were among the featured performers. Those games formed part of a regional football night that included championship stakes, a rivalry shutout and weather interruptions. On the Treasure Coast, the district picture was the main focus: Vero Beach celebrated its District 8-6A title, while Jensen Beach’s meeting with Fort Pierce Westwood carried the District 13-4A championship stakes.

hero.headline: ACLU Letter Alleges Abuse, Medical Neglect at 'Deportation Depot' Facility
hero.body:
The ACLU and other advocacy groups have filed a letter alleging widespread abuse of detainees at the Florida immigration detention facility known as "Deportation Depot." The groups say they conducted dozens of interviews with people currently or recently detained at the facility, their loved ones, and attorneys who represent detainees there, and that those interviews point to a pattern of serious abuse.

The letter identifies seven categories of abuse: life-threatening medical neglect; lack of adequate food and clean drinking water; excessive, life-threatening heat; squalid, unsanitary, and unsafe living conditions; deprivation of necessities for physical, mental, and emotional wellbeing such as sleep, family visitation, and outdoor recreation; verbal and physical abuse and retaliation; and lack of access to the courts and to confidential communication with attorneys. On the issue of food, the letter states that detainees are not given enough nutritious food, describing portions as "extremely small, infant-sized food portions that are not filling" that lack adequate protein or nutrients. It cites cases of dramatic weight loss, including one detainee who lost 29 pounds in less than two months and another who lost 44 pounds over seven months.

On water, the letter alleges the facility does not provide adequate access to clean drinking water. It says the only water available in the dorms most of the time comes from visibly rusty fountains, and that newly arrived detainees are warned by others not to drink from them because many people have gotten sick doing so. One former detainee named Ryan said he and others would try to drink as much water as possible from the cafeteria during their brief mealtimes because it was the only source of clean water. He said that in the dorms, "you had no alternative sometimes than just to kind of take your chances with the water," describing it as having "a very strong metallic taste" that made his stomach feel like "something was kicking and punching" it once it settled.

ACLU attorney Amy Godshall, who wrote the letter, said the facility appears designed to strip detainees of basic dignity. "It's very much a cruel facility that's designed to deny people every aspect of humanity and decency and dignity, and is designed to make people physically weak, mentally weak, and just pressured to agree to the point where they agree to self deportation," she said. The letter argues this pressure may be intentional, stating there is evidence of a deliberate effort to make detention conditions unbearable so that people give up their legal rights and accept removal, adding that whether or not the conditions are intentional, they are punitive and unconstitutional. Ryan said he was approached by guards on three or four separate occasions and asked to sign forms consenting to his own deportation. "The question that a lot of us had is, well, if we were deportable, then why would we have to sign this document to make us deportable?" he said.

When Alligator Alcatraz shut down over the summer, it didn't end Florida's involvement in immigration detention. There's a second state-run facility that's been open for a year in a former prison about 50 minutes west of Jacksonville. Because its location is less controversial than the Everglades, it's flown largely under the radar. But now, detainees are speaking up about the alleged horrors inside what state officials have dubbed 'Deportation Depot.' 'It's insane. There's no other word [to describe the situation] than insanity. Just how bad these conditions were,' said a man who asked that we hide his face and refer to him by his middle name, Ryan. He fears being publicly identified could jeopardize his still-pending immigration case. 'I'm happy to be here, and I'm grateful, and obviously I'm gonna do everything I can to complete my immigration journey, and hopefully I can put this behind me,' Ryan said. I learned from the American Civil Liberties Union and confirmed through federal court records and local news reports that Ryan was detained by immigration authorities in late February and sent to the Baker Correctional Institution in Sanderson, where he spent four months. According to the most recent ICE detention data from July, roughly a thousand migrant men are housed at Baker. The ACLU put the number even higher, at about 1,200, during Ryan's stay. 'They were businessmen, entrepreneurs, paramedics, people that had been in the military. It was just, it was just everyone,' Ryan said. Ryan told me about 100 people in his dorm, with four working toilets and four working showers. He described the bathrooms as filthy, toiletries as scarce, and extreme heat as a persistent problem. hero.headline: Jensen Beach's Andrew Burnette wins legal fight for fifth year, returns to Louisiana Tech
hero.body:
Jensen Beach native Andrew Burnette has won back a fifth season of college football eligibility after taking his case to court against the NCAA, and he is now back on the field at Louisiana Tech. Burnette moved to Martin County from Michigan around age 12 and went on to star at Jensen Beach High School, where he originally enrolled to wrestle before football took over as his main focus. "I wasn't zoned for that school, but I went there for wrestling originally; that was my first passion," Burnette said. "Moving through high school, I knew football was what I wanted to do."

Despite his success at Jensen Beach High School, Burnette said he did not draw much interest from college recruiters, a common experience for Treasure Coast football players. "One of my main struggles was recruitment out of high school, because I felt like our area was a little under-recruited," he said. He chose to play at Highland Community College in Kansas, where he rushed for 340 yards and two touchdowns in nine games, but still failed to attract bigger programs. He then transferred to Independence Junior College, a school featured on the Netflix series Last Chance U, but was cut from that team.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies on Duty, Brother Died in 2025
hero.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge died on duty Saturday, just over a year after his brother Jarius died while serving in the same role. The Hodge family had publicly pushed for accountability after Jarius's 2025 death at a Port St. Lucie hospital.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge died while on duty Saturday, Oct. 24, more than a year after his younger brother Jarius Hodge, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died at age 26. The district announced Austin's line-of-duty death Saturday, calling it a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Austin Hodge had joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years, most recently assigned to Station 9. Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue also shared condolences following his unexpected death Saturday morning. The circumstances surrounding Austin's death have not been released, and the fire district asked the public to respect his family's privacy as they grieve.

Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025, after becoming ill with the flu he contracted from a patient at work earlier that month. Austin said his brother had been healthy before getting sick and alleged that medical staff made critical errors in his treatment, including taking three attempts to intubate him.

The brothers shared a close bond built around their shared career in firefighting. "This was my best friend, my twin," Austin said of Jarius in the earlier interview. "We had the same hairstyle." He described his brother as someone who loved going to work and loved working alongside him. "He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him," Austin said. "He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country."

After Jarius's death, Austin spoke publicly about Florida's medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability. "This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long," Austin said. He stressed that the family wanted accountability, not money. "For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar," he said. "We just want those physicians to be held accountable." The St. Lucie County Fire District said it will share information about memorial arrangements and ways to honor Austin Hodge's service once details are finalized in coordination with his family.

cards.teaser: A geofence warrant and matching vehicle fasteners helped detectives crack the two-week case, but police say they are still looking for a second vehicle.
cards.body:

Police also recovered pieces of the vehicle's inner fender-well fasteners at the scene and found that several matching fasteners were missing from Aude's vehicle.

The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. 9 on NW California Boulevard just south of the intersection with NW University Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the road with severe head injuries and remains in critical condition at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Ft. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested Eric Saint Aude on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. He said Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash happened. Investigators reviewed video, physical evidence and other leads since the crash two weeks ago. Niemczyk said a geofence warrant which sought cellphone location data from a specific area during a specific time produced a lead showing Aude's phone had pinged off cell phone towers in that area at the time of the crash. That helped detectives identify Aude as the alleged hit and run driver and the vehicles registered to him. Detectives then located and examined the man’s vehicle, which had damage consistent with striking a pedestrian, including damage to the front bumper and hood, Niemczyk said. Investigators also found presumptive positive results for blood on the vehicle. Further testing is needed. Police also recovered pieces of the vehicle’s inner fender-well fasteners at the scene, Niemczyk said. Detectives found that several matching fasteners were missing from the suspect’s vehicle. Investigators are still looking for a second vehicle that was traveling southbound near the crash. Niemczyk said distant video showed a vehicle traveling in each direction, but it was difficult to determine what happened. Police are trying to learn whether the second vehicle also struck the victim or if the driver of the second vehicle witnessed the accident. We’re very confident that the vehicle that we have and the person that we’ve arrested are responsible for the majority of what occurred, Niemczyk said. The Police Chief said the victim was in the middle of the road when he was struck, but investigators could not determine from the video whether he was walking or jogging. Police learned he often exercised at night when the weather was cooler and he was known to walk on the road and medians. "I've been doing this for 30 years. I'm not surprised by a whole lot anymore. I've seen pedestrians left for dead on the side of the road before. It doesn't make it any easier, but it doesn't surprise me at this point either. It's just difficult to understand how one human being could be so, you know, without compassion for another," Chief Niemczyk said. See also: 2 arrested in killing of transgender woman Jayla McGee in Belle Glade The victim had no identification or cellphone with him, Niemczyk said. Investigators used data from a Garmin exercise watch he was wearing to trace his route back to his house and were able to identify him. Niemczyk said the victim has significant head trauma and is unable to speak. He is expected to survive, but the chief said his quality of life may not be the same as it was before the crash. "An arrest cannot undo the harm or uncertainty imposed upon a victim, Niemczyk said, but it’s the first step in accountability. Police have not released a description of the southbound vehicle. Anyone with information is asked to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000. Aude is being held on $45,000 bond.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies on Duty, One Year After Brother's Death
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter/paramedic Austin Hodge, 34, died Saturday morning while on duty, the agency said. His death comes one year after his brother, Jarius Hodge, also a firefighter with the district, died after falling ill at work.

Austin Hodge joined the St. Lucie County Fire District on July 17, 2017, and was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce. On Saturday morning, a procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies escorted him from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce. The St. Lucie County Fire District called his death "a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community," and extended "heartfelt condolences to Hodge's family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time."

Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at Station 3, where he worked. His family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. On May 30, people gathered to celebrate what would have been his 27th birthday with a cookout and balloon release. cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Arrest Man in Oct. 9 Hit-and-Run That Critically Injured Nighttime Exerciser
cards.teaser: Detectives used surveillance video and the victim's Garmin watch data to identify Eric Saint Aude as a suspect in the crash near NW University and NW California boulevards.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested Eric Saint Aude in connection with an Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old man in critical condition near NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard. The crash happened around 12:56 a.m. and left the victim unconscious in the roadway with severe head injuries.

Police said the victim, who was out exercising at the time, was a familiar sight to officers working the night shift. "Our officers that work night we're used to seeing him out exercising in the evening and he was known to jog, walk in the street medians," Port St. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said. The man was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where he remains in critical condition.

Investigators identified the victim using information from his Garmin watch, which was traced back to his home. Detectives then reviewed surveillance video and gathered additional evidence that led them to identify Saint Aude, 60, as a suspect in the crash.

Saint Aude was arrested on a charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, according to Port St. Lucie police.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Police: Missing 5-Year-Old Found Dead in Pond Near Portofino Landing
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police say a 5-year-old nonverbal girl who went missing from her apartment complex Saturday was found dead hours later in a nearby pond, with investigators now revealing new details about the search effort, including an attempt to track her location through a tablet she had with her. Mayra Glory Odelus was last seen before noon in the 5100 block of Portofino Landing Apartments east of Interstate 95. Her body was discovered in the pond at about 3 p.m., roughly 75 yards from her apartment, about three hours after she was reported missing. Police received the initial report at 11:39 a.m., and family members told officers Mayra was autistic and nonverbal.

She was last seen wearing a dark oversized shirt with two white beads in her hair. Officers searched the surrounding area, handed out flyers with her name and photo, and flew drones over the area. Police called in Port St. Lucie bloodhounds and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office dive team, which conducted an underwater search that led to the discovery of her body. According to police spokesperson Michael Santiago, Mayra had a tablet with her when she disappeared, and her family tried to locate her by pinging the device. The ping led searchers to the pond area, but at that point there was no sign of her, and the tablet itself has still not been recovered.

Mayra's father told police the pond sits directly across from their apartment and that she loved the water. He and Mayra's 18-year-old sister were home at the time she went missing. Her mother lives in Haiti and was expected to arrive Sunday. "Our deepest condolences are with Mayra's family and loved ones during this tragic time," the Fort Pierce Police Department said in a statement. Santiago added, "It's very tragic when anything like this happens, but with our kids we have to make sure we're paying attention all the time, especially when kids are challenged with autism."

Drowning remains the leading cause of unintentional death among children ages 1 to 3. Dr. Elizabeth Feldman of Cleveland Clinic Florida has said drowning can happen within seconds, and a lack of oxygen for just a few minutes can cause brain injury. The Children's Services Council of Palm Beach reported that 39 children with autism or suspected autism drowned in Florida in 2025, the highest number ever recorded in the state. The case has renewed attention on tracking and safety devices designed to prevent or respond to water-related emergencies involving children with autism, many of whom are drawn to water and may wander from supervision without being able to call for help.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies on Duty, Year After Brother's Death
cards.teaser: Austin Hodge, a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic who publicly pushed for medical malpractice accountability after his brother's 2025 death, died while on duty Saturday.
cards.body:
A St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic died while on duty Saturday morning, more than a year after his younger brother, who also served as a firefighter-paramedic for the district, died at age 26. The St. Lucie County Fire District announced the line-of-duty death of Austin Hodge on Saturday, Oct. 24, calling it a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years. He was assigned to Station 9. Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue also shared condolences following his unexpected death. The circumstances surrounding Austin Hodge's death have not been released. The fire district asked the public to respect his family's privacy as they grieve and said information about memorial arrangements will be shared once finalized.

Austin Hodge's death comes more than a year after his younger brother, Jarius Hodge, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died on July 22, 2025. The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. "We had the same hairstyle." He described Jarius as someone who loved his family and his work as a first responder. "He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him," Austin said. "He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country."

In that earlier interview, Austin said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025. He said his brother went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22, struggling to breathe, but died hours later. Austin alleged that medical staff made critical errors in treating Jarius, including taking three attempts to intubate him, and said his brother had been healthy before becoming ill.

Austin also spoke publicly about Florida's medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability for his brother's death. "This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long," he said. He emphasized that his family was seeking accountability rather than financial compensation. "For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar," he said. "We just want those physicians to be held accountable." The St. Lucie County Fire District said additional information about ways to honor Austin Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family.

hero.headline: Martin County Approves School Zone for Citrus Grove Elementary After 5-Year Push
hero.body:
Martin County commissioners have unanimously approved a new school zone on Southwest Newfield Parkway outside Citrus Grove Elementary School, answering years of safety concerns from parents who say the current 45 mph speed limit puts children at risk. Many families whose children walk to school live in the Canopy Creek community across the street from the elementary school.

Kelly Ribaudo, the school's PTA president and Martin County PTA Advocacy Chair, said she has spent the last five years asking the county to install a school zone. "We've had so many near misses with the kids just from people not paying attention," Ribaudo said. "Everyone has a right to a free and public education and they should be safe getting there. Our main priority should be the kids not the traffic." Parent Kendall George said the current traffic conditions are frightening. "It scares me," George said. "These cars are driving 45 miles an hour plus."

At a previous Martin County Commission meeting, commissioners sided with the parents. "Whatever the number is there is no price to someone getting hurt," Martin County Commissioner Edward Ciampi said. "You will absolutely get a school zone." School Principal Rose Rynca said the need has grown as new communities have developed in the area and enrollment has increased. "The amount of students crossing Newfield Parkway has definitely increased," Rynca said. "This speed zone is going to really really improve the safety of students." George said a marked school zone will help remind drivers to be careful. "It's letting drivers know that, hey there's a school here, there's children crossing, and we have to slow down," George said.

The county was asked this week for a timeline on when the school zone will be installed on Southwest Newfield Parkway. In the meantime, parents are urging drivers to use caution near the school regardless of posted signage. "Slow down if you see a school, even if there's not a school zone sign, slow down," Ribaudo said. With the school zone now approved, parents say their next priority is pushing the county for improved street lighting in the area.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Police: Nonverbal 5-Year-Old Found Dead in Pond Near Portofino Landing
hero.body:
A 5-year-old nonverbal autistic girl who disappeared from her Fort Pierce apartment complex on Saturday was found dead hours later in a nearby pond, and police say she had a tablet with her that her family tried to use to locate her before she was found. Mayra Glory Odelus was last seen before noon in the 5100 block of Portofino Landing Apartments, east of Interstate 95. Her body was recovered at about 3 p.m. in a pond directly across from her family's apartment, roughly three hours after she was reported missing.

Police said they received the report of Mayra missing at 11:39 a.m. Officers searched the surrounding area, distributed flyers with her name and photo, and launched drones over the complex. The department called in Port St. Lucie bloodhounds and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office dive team, which ultimately found her in the pond. Mayra was last seen wearing a dark oversized shirt with two white beads in her hair. Her father told police the pond sat directly across from their home and that she loved the water. He and Mayra's 18-year-old sister were home at the time she went missing. Her mother, who lives in Haiti, was expected to arrive in Fort Pierce on Sunday. "Our deepest condolences are with Mayra's family and loved ones during this tragic time," the police department said.

Officials said the family attempted to track Mayra by pinging a tablet she had with her when she disappeared. According to Michael Santiago, the signal led searchers to the area where they were standing, but there was no sign of the girl there, and the tablet itself still has not been recovered. "It's very tragic when anything like this happens, but with our kids we have to make sure we're paying attention all the time, especially when kids are challenged with autism," Santiago said.

The case highlights a broader danger facing children with autism. The Children's Services Council of Palm Beach reported that 39 children with autism or suspected autism drowned in Florida in 2025, the highest number ever recorded in the state. Drowning remains the leading cause of unintentional death among young children. Medical experts note how quickly it can turn fatal. Dr. Elizabeth Feldman of Cleveland Clinic Florida said drowning can happen in as little as 20 to 30 seconds, and a lack of oxygen can cause brain injury within minutes. Specialized tracking devices and water safety tools are increasingly used by families of children with autism to help prevent these kinds of tragedies or respond quickly when a child goes missing near water.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies, Brother Died in Same Job in 2025
cards.teaser: Austin Hodge, a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic for more than nine years, died in the line of duty Saturday, just over a year after his younger brother Jarius died while serving in the same department.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge died while on duty Saturday, more than a year after his younger brother Jarius, who also served as a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died at age 26. The St. Lucie County Fire District announced Hodge's death on Saturday, Oct. 24, calling it a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years. He was assigned to Station 9. Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue also shared condolences following his unexpected death Saturday morning. The circumstances surrounding Austin Hodge's death have not been released.

Austin Hodge's death comes more than a year after his brother Jarius Hodge, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died on July 22, 2025. The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. "We had the same hairstyle." He described Jarius as someone who loved his family and his work as a first responder. "He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him," Austin said. "He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country."

In that earlier interview, Austin said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025. Austin said his younger brother went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22, struggling to breathe, and died hours later. He alleged that medical staff made critical errors in treating his brother, including taking three attempts to intubate him, and said Jarius had been healthy before becoming ill.

Austin also spoke publicly about Florida's medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability for Jarius's death. "This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long," Austin said. He emphasized that his family was seeking accountability rather than financial compensation. "For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar," he said. "We just want those physicians to be held accountable." The St. Lucie County Fire District asked the public to respect the Hodge family as they grieve and said information about memorial arrangements and ways to honor Austin Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family once details are finalized.

cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District announced the line-of-duty death of firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge on Saturday, just over a year after his brother Jarius Hodge died following disputed hospital treatment.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District announced the line-of-duty death of firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge on Saturday, Oct. 24, more than a year after his younger brother and fellow firefighter-paramedic, Jarius Hodge, died at age 26. The district called Austin Hodge's death a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, served the community for more than nine years and was assigned to Station 9. Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue also shared condolences following his unexpected death Saturday morning. The circumstances surrounding his death have not been released.

Austin Hodge's death comes more than a year after Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025. The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. "This was my best friend, my twin," Austin Hodge previously said. "We had the same hairstyle." He described Jarius as someone who loved his family and his work as a first responder. "He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him," Austin said. "He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country."

Austin had said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025. Jarius went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22, struggling to breathe, and died hours later. Austin alleged that medical staff made critical errors treating his brother, including taking three attempts to intubate him, and said Jarius had been healthy before becoming ill.

Austin also spoke publicly about Florida's medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability for Jarius's death. "This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long," Austin said. He emphasized that his family was seeking accountability rather than financial compensation. "For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar," he said. "We just want those physicians to be held accountable." St. Lucie County Fire District asked the public to respect the Hodge family's privacy as they grieve and said information about memorial arrangements and ways to honor Austin Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Fire District Mourns Second Hodge Brother in a Year
hero.body:
A firefighter-paramedic with the St. Lucie County Fire District died Saturday morning while on duty, just over a year after his brother, also a member of the department, died in similar circumstances. Austin Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years. He was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce.

Austin's brother, Jarius Hodge, died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at work at Station 3. His family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. On May 30, friends and family gathered for a cookout and balloon release to celebrate what would have been Jarius's 27th birthday. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today."

On Saturday, a procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies escorted Austin Hodge from the hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce. The St. Lucie County Fire District, which operates 20 fire stations with 523 firefighters, said in a statement that his death "is a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community" and extended "heartfelt condolences to Hodge's family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time." The district said information about memorial arrangements and ways to honor Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized.

The department also thanked agencies across the region for their support in the hours after the loss. In a Facebook post, the district wrote, "In the hours following this heartbreaking loss, our firefighters, Honor Guard, and public safety partners came together to honor our fallen brother and stand alongside one another during an incredibly difficult time. The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station. It is a bond built on trust, shared experiences, and an unwavering commitment to one another. Today, that bond was especially evident through the incredible support of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties. Together, they offered strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves. Our hearts are with Austin's family, loved ones, and everyone who had the privilege of serving alongside him. We are deeply grateful to our fellow first responders and community for the outpouring of support during this tremendous loss." Condolences also came from Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, the Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, the Port St. Lucie Police Department, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Riviera Beach Fire Rescue. The district also lost firefighter Connor Whitehead, 21, who died on May 31.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies On Duty A Year After Brother's Death
cards.teaser: Austin Hodge died while on duty Saturday, 15 months after his younger brother Jarius died following treatment at Cleveland Clinic Tradition in Port St. Lucie. Austin had publicly pushed for accountability over his brother's death and criticized Florida's medical malpractice laws.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge died while on duty Saturday, more than a year after his younger brother Jarius, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died at age 26. The St. Lucie County Fire District announced Hodge's line-of-duty death on Oct. 24, calling it a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, served the community for more than nine years, and was assigned to Station 9. The circumstances surrounding his death have not been released.

Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue shared condolences following Hodge's unexpected death Saturday morning. The St. Lucie County Fire District asked the public to respect Hodge's family as they grieve and said additional information about memorial arrangements and ways to honor his service will be shared in coordination with the family once finalized.

Hodge's death comes more than a year after his brother Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025. The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. "We had the same hairstyle." He described Jarius as someone who loved his family and his work as a first responder. "He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him," Austin said. "He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country."

In that earlier interview, Austin said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025 and went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22 struggling to breathe, but died hours later. Austin alleged that medical staff made critical errors in treating his brother, including taking three attempts to intubate him, and said Jarius had been healthy before becoming ill. Austin also spoke publicly about Florida's medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability for Jarius' death. "This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long," Austin said. He emphasized that his family sought accountability rather than financial compensation. "For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar," he said. "We just want those physicians to be held accountable."

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Arrest Man in Oct. 9 Hit-and-Run That Critically Injured Jogger
hero.teaser: Detectives used surveillance video and the victim's Garmin watch data to identify a suspect in the hit-and-run that left a 63-year-old man with severe head injuries. Eric Saint Aude, 60, has been arrested on a charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a man in connection with an Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old jogger critically injured. Eric Saint Aude, 60, was taken into custody and charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

The crash happened around 12:56 a.m. near NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard. Officers found the 63-year-old man unconscious in the roadway with severe head injuries. He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital and remains in critical condition.

Investigators identified the victim using information from his Garmin watch, which they traced back to his home. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said night-shift officers were familiar with the victim from his regular exercise routine. "Our officers that work night we're used to seeing him out exercising in the evening and he was known to jog, walk in the street medians," Niemczyk said.

Detectives reviewed surveillance video along with additional evidence to identify Saint Aude as a suspect in the crash. That investigative work led to his arrest on the hit-and-run charge, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

hero.headline: FHP Report: Freightliner Turned Into SUV's Path in Fatal Indian River Crash
hero.body:
A newly released Florida Highway Patrol report details how a 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday when the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. The traffic homicide investigation remains open, and the man's next of kin had not been notified as of the report.

According to the crash report, a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer was stopped at a stop sign on westbound 49th Street and attempted to turn left when it entered the path of a northbound 2006 Dodge Durango traveling on 66th Avenue. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the trailer.

The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. The 59-year-old Jacksonville man driving the Freightliner did not report any injuries.

Florida Highway Patrol's traffic homicide investigation into the crash is ongoing.

hero.headline: FHP Report Details Fatal Semi Crash at 66th Ave and 49th St in Indian River County
hero.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday after the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. A newly released Florida Highway Patrol crash report details how the collision unfolded and confirms the man's next of kin had not yet been notified as of the report.

According to the report, a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer was stopped at a stop sign on westbound 49th Street when it attempted to turn left. The Freightliner entered the path of a 2006 Dodge Durango traveling north on 66th Avenue. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the trailer.

The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. The 59-year-old Jacksonville man who was driving the Freightliner did not report any injuries.

The Florida Highway Patrol's traffic homicide investigation into the crash is ongoing.

hero.headline: Bronx Man Extradited to St. Lucie County in Check Fraud, Money Laundering Case
hero.teaser: Detectives traced a stolen, altered check from a Port St. Lucie real estate company through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers before linking it to a 22-year-old New York man.
hero.body:
A 22-year-old man from the Bronx has been extradited to St. Lucie County to face charges after detectives linked him to a check stolen from a Port St. Lucie real estate company and funneled through a money laundering scheme, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said Friday. Gibrill Diallo faces charges of money laundering between $300 and $20,000, scheme to defraud of $50,000 or more, and grand theft.

The Sheriff's Office Economic Crimes Unit launched a multi-jurisdictional investigation after a check mailed by the Port St. Lucie real estate company was stolen and fraudulently altered. The check was deposited into a bank account opened using a stolen identity, according to the Sheriff's Office. Detectives then traced the money as it moved through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers, which investigators say were used to disguise where the funds originated, before the money landed in Diallo's personal bank account.

Diallo was apprehended on Oct. 14 by Canadian border authorities as he attempted to enter Canada from the United States. He was held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before being extradited to St. Lucie County on Wednesday at 9:39 p.m. Bond was set at a total of $30,000 across the three charges.

"Our detectives followed the money, uncovered a complex financial scheme, and pursued every lead until the suspect was brought back to St. Lucie County to face justice," St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said in a statement. "This case reflects the relentless investigative work and determination of our Economic Crimes Unit. Our residents and businesses work hard for what they earn, and they deserve to know that when someone tries to take advantage of them, our detectives will go the extra mile to hold those responsible accountable."

County officials said the donations will support families in need throughout St. Lucie County through the Treasure Coast Food Bank's distribution network.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Fire District Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee in 4-3 Vote
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against his leadership. The board appointed Paul Langel, a 30-year veteran of the district, as interim chief following the decision.

The termination comes two months after five firefighters were displaced for allegedly turning a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and using it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three firefighters ultimately lost their jobs over the incident. The disciplined firefighters have called their termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership.

Langel said he sees his new role as a chance to move the department forward. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job. Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process," he said. Asked whether the terminated firefighters could get their jobs back, Langel did not rule it out. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen. I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics," he said.

Jordon Hutchinson, one of the firefighters terminated in the hazing case, said he welcomed the board's decision to remove Lee. "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department," he said. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early. The question of whether the three fired firefighters could be reinstated remains unresolved as Langel settles into his new role.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Mayor's Race, Trash Pickup Question Top Nov. Ballot
hero.body:
Early voting is underway in Port St. Lucie, where voters will decide a tense mayoral race between incumbent Shannon Martin and challenger Steven Giordano, along with a non-binding ballot question asking whether the city should switch to twice-a-week trash pickup, a change that would cost residents more than $100 a year. Election day is less than two weeks away.

On the first day of early voting, campaign tents for Martin and Giordano stood side by side outside a polling location on Rosser Boulevard, reflecting what has become a bitter contest. Martin is running for another term and argues the city should stay on its current course, pointing to infrastructure work, including roadwork, as evidence her administration is delivering results. Giordano has accused City Hall of corruption and of losing touch with everyday residents. When asked what he would do differently, he also pointed to roadwork, saying the city needs a new traffic study. Port St. Lucie's mayor serves a four-year term and holds significant power under the city's mayor-council form of government. Neither candidate is running with a party affiliation, since the mayoral race is nonpartisan.

The ballot also asks voters whether the city should add a second weekly trash collection day. FCC handles garbage collection in Port St. Lucie. The question will not bind the city council, which could choose to ignore the outcome regardless of how residents vote. At recent city council meetings, residents have complained that current trash service is inadequate and have pushed for an additional pickup day. Resident Rob Buske offered a different view, saying, "I don't want to pay for something I don't need." On the first day of early voting, people asked about the issue said they would rather keep the current one-day pickup schedule, even as others have demanded a change.

The trash question, like the mayoral race, is nonpartisan, but both issues have generated strong feelings among residents. The choice over who leads the city comes down to differing visions for Port St. Lucie's direction, while the trash question centers on a simpler, more immediate concern: how often garbage gets picked up at the curb. Both items will appear on the same ballot as voters decide the city's near-term direction over the next two weeks.

Investigators reviewed video, physical evidence and other leads since the crash two weeks ago. Detectives then located and examined the man’s vehicle, which had damage consistent with striking a pedestrian, including damage to the front bumper and hood, Niemczyk said. Investigators also found presumptive positive results for blood on the vehicle. Further testing is needed. Police also recovered pieces of the vehicle’s inner fender-well fasteners at the scene, Niemczyk said. Detectives found that several matching fasteners were missing from the suspect’s vehicle. Investigators are still looking for a second vehicle that was traveling southbound near the crash. Niemczyk said distant video showed a vehicle traveling in each direction, but it was difficult to determine what happened. Police are trying to learn whether the second vehicle also struck the victim or if the driver of the second vehicle witnessed the accident. We’re very confident that the vehicle that we have and the person that we’ve arrested are responsible for the majority of what occurred, Niemczyk said. Police learned he often exercised at night when the weather was cooler and he was known to walk on the road and medians. "I've been doing this for 30 years. I'm not surprised by a whole lot anymore. I've seen pedestrians left for dead on the side of the road before. It doesn't make it any easier, but it doesn't surprise me at this point either. Investigators used data from a Garmin exercise watch he was wearing to trace his route back to his house and were able to identify him. "An arrest cannot undo the harm or uncertainty imposed upon a victim, Niemczyk said, but it’s the first step in accountability. Police have not released a description of the southbound vehicle. cards.body:
A 22-year-old New York man is facing charges in St. Lucie County after a multi-jurisdictional investigation into an organized check fraud and money laundering scheme, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said Friday. Gibrill Diallo, of the Bronx, was arrested after detectives with the Sheriff's Office Economic Crimes Unit traced stolen funds from a Port St. Lucie real estate company back to his personal bank account.

According to the Sheriff's Office, a check mailed by the real estate company was stolen, fraudulently altered and deposited into a bank account set up using a stolen identity. Detectives said the stolen funds were then moved through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers in an effort to conceal their origin before ending up in Diallo's personal account. Investigators obtained an arrest warrant charging Diallo with money laundering between $300 and $20,000, scheme to defraud of $50,000 or more, and grand theft.

On Oct. 14, Canadian border authorities apprehended Diallo as he attempted to enter Canada from the United States. He was held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before being extradited to St. Lucie County on Wednesday at 9:39 p.m. Bond on the three charges was set at a combined $30,000.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro credited the Economic Crimes Unit for the arrest. “Our detectives followed the money, uncovered a complex financial scheme, and pursued every lead until the suspect was brought back to St. Lucie County to face justice,” Del Toro said in a statement. "This case reflects the relentless investigative work and determination of our Economic Crimes Unit. Our residents and businesses work hard for what they earn, and they deserve to know that when someone tries to take advantage of them, our detectives will go the extra mile to hold those responsible accountable.”

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee in 4-3 Vote
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause following a hazing scandal and a no-confidence vote, and named interim Chief Paul Langel to lead the department.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, following months of controversy, hazing allegations, and a no-confidence vote against him. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early.

The board appointed Paul Langel as interim chief. Langel has 30 years of experience in the district and is a familiar face there. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job," Langel said. "Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process."

The termination comes two months after five firefighters were displaced over allegations that they turned a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and used it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three firefighters ultimately lost their jobs over the incident. Those disciplined firefighters have called Lee's termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership. One of the terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson, offered a different view of the board's decision. "I think it was a step in the right direction," Hutchinson said. "I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department."

Asked whether the terminated firefighters could get their jobs back, Langel did not rule it out but said he needs time to learn the details of the cases. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen," he said. "I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics."

hero.headline: Leon County probe: CBP agents at polling site tried to vote, not enforce
hero.body:
Leon County election officials and the FBI have concluded that Customs and Border Protection agents seen near an early voting site this week were mistakenly trying to vote before leaving the state, not conducting an immigration enforcement action. A separate incident involving an armed arrest near a Key Largo polling place remains under review by Monroe County election officials. Both episodes drew scrutiny because federal law bars armed officers or troops from operating near polling places, and the Trump administration has repeatedly assured election officials that federal agents would not be stationed at voting sites.

The Leon County incident began Monday when two CBP vehicles parked outside the Northeast Branch Library, described by county election supervisor Mark Earley as the busiest early voting site in the county. The vehicles stayed about 10 minutes before leaving. Earley said his office received no calls from voters about the incident, but he filed a complaint with the FBI because voters may experience intimidation. On Friday, Earley's office said the county sheriff's office and FBI determined the vehicles belonged to a team of agents normally stationed in south Florida who had been reassigned to another state. While driving north to their new post, they stopped at the last Florida polling place on their route after realizing they would not be in the state on Election Day. Earley said the agents mistakenly believed they could vote there, even though they were not Leon County voters, and left immediately once they learned otherwise. He said he accepts that account and considers it an isolated incident consistent with assurances that federal agents would not be stationed at polling sites.

A CBP spokesperson said the officers were traveling in a government vehicle from Florida to Brownsville, Texas, in support of an out-of-state deployment, and that the stop was not an immigration enforcement action. The officers, who were out of uniform, asked whether they could vote early before leaving the state and were told they were only eligible to vote in their home county. The spokesperson said the officers thanked staff and promptly departed, and that government personnel, like all eligible Americans, may exercise their right to vote.

The second incident occurred Tuesday outside the Murray Nelson Government Center in Key Largo, where a community group posted video showing masked and armed federal agents conducting what appeared to be a traffic stop near the polling site. A representative of the group 50501 Key Largo said it was unclear why the agents were there and raised concern that their presence could intimidate voters. Monroe County election supervisor Sherri Hodies said CBP told her agents were trying to pull over a suspect who turned toward the government center, and her office is investigating. A CBP spokesperson said Border Patrol agents assigned to the Marathon Station stopped a vehicle on U.S. Highway 1 as part of a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Arwiin Pillay, described as a Malaysian national in the country illegally with prior charges for drug possession and battery. The spokesperson said the driver pulled into a parking lot adjacent to the polling location, where agents arrested Pillay and left shortly after. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has said agents would only be present at polling places if there were a threat to the site or if they were serving a warrant on someone they were actively tracking.

hero.headline: PSLPD Arrest in NW California Boulevard Hit-and-Run, Second Vehicle Sought
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a man in connection with the Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old Port St. Lucie resident in critical condition, and investigators are still trying to identify a second vehicle that may have also been involved. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested 60-year-old Eric Saint Aude on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. Aude is being held on $45,000 bond.

The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. on Oct. 9 on NW California Boulevard just south of the intersection with NW University Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the road with severe head injuries and remains at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce. Niemczyk said Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash happened.

Detectives built the case using video, physical evidence and other leads gathered over the two weeks since the crash. A geofence warrant seeking cellphone location data from the crash area at the time of the collision showed Aude's phone had pinged off cell towers there, which helped investigators identify him and the vehicles registered to him. When detectives examined Aude's vehicle, they found damage to the front bumper and hood consistent with striking a pedestrian, along with presumptive positive results for blood, though further testing is needed. Police also recovered pieces of an inner fender-well fastener at the scene and found that matching fasteners were missing from Aude's vehicle.
